document.title: Politburo Session, February 23, 1987
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: Gorbachev discusses withdrawing while engaging the US and Pakistan in negotiations on a final settlement. He is willing to meet Pakistani leader Zia ul Haq, maybe offering a payoff, and worries about Soviet reputation among non-aligned countries and national liberation movements.

persons.name: Andrei Gromyko
persons.role: CPSU Politburo member; Soviet statesman arguing for ending the war and a negotiated troop withdrawal

mentions.quote: The Mujahadeen are getting stronger. We aren't able to use our tanks in the mountains.
We need to send our representative to the negotiations between the Pakistanis and Cordovez, maybe Kryuchkov.

persons.name: Eduard Shevardnadze
persons.role: Soviet foreign minister and Politburo participant; argues a pullout is not possible in under two years and that Najibullah must not fall

mentions.quote: A pullout will not be possible in under two years.
Most important is that we do not allow the Najibullah regime to fall.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CPSU, chairing the Politburo session

mentions.quote: We must keep Nadjibulla in power- that much is a necessity.
maybe we should even invite Zia-ul-Khaq (the Pakistani president) to meet with me in Tashkent

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: Leader of the Afghan government (PDPA regime) supported by the USSR

mentions.quote: Najibullah has said that, supposedly, Gorbachev has promised to bring in another 500,000 men to Afghanistan.

persons.name: Diego Cordovez
persons.role: UN mediator in negotiations on Afghanistan

mentions.quote: If this round of negotiations with Cordovez is fruitless, it will just lead to a consolidation of the Mujahadeen's position.

persons.name: Vladimir Kryuchkov
persons.role: Suggested Soviet representative to the Pakistan–Cordovez negotiations (KGB official)

mentions.quote: We need to send our representative to the negotiations between the Pakistanis and Cordovez, maybe Kryuchkov.

persons.name: Zia-ul-Haq
persons.role: President of Pakistan; proposed invitee to meet Gorbachev in Tashkent

mentions.quote: maybe we should even invite Zia-ul-Khaq (the Pakistani president) to meet with me in Tashkent, and maybe even 'pay' him

events.description: CPSU Politburo session discussing Afghanistan, negotiations with Cordovez, withdrawal timetable and keeping Najibullah in power.
Proposal by Gorbachev to invite Zia-ul-Haq to Tashkent and possibly make concessions.
CPSU Politburo session discusses Afghanistan withdrawal timetable, Cordovez talks, and keeping Najibullah in power; decides to continue negotiations.
Gorbachev floats inviting Zia-ul-Haq to Tashkent and making deals with the Americans.
Gromyko proposes sending Kryuchkov to the Pakistan–Cordovez negotiations.

key_claims: Gromyko told the Politburo the Mujahadeen were growing stronger and Soviet tanks were ineffective in the mountains.
Gromyko considered closing the Afghanistan-Pakistan border impossible and urged ending the war via agreement.
Shevardnadze argued a Soviet pullout would take at least two years and the Najibullah regime must not fall.
Gorbachev insisted on keeping Najibullah in power while keeping negotiations alive and possibly conceding on the withdrawal schedule.
Gorbachev floated deals with the Americans and inviting Zia-ul-Haq to Tashkent, possibly with payment.
